text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:
- Three Singapore Armed Forces servicemen received a new State award for bravery during an accident in New Zealand on March 9 in which two soldiers died and 12 others were injured.
- Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen said Phnom Penh might withdraw its application to join ASEAN if the group continued to interfere in the country's internal affairs.
- Hun Sen confirmed the killing of a senior intelligence officer, the second official loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh to be killed since the prince's ouster.

- Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's dispatch of three Japanese military transport planes to Thailand, where they are on standby for the possible evacuation of Japanese from Cambodia, has been criticised by one of his coalition partners as "illegal" and by Japanese in Phnom Penh as "meaningless".
- A Singapore student has been left paralysed from the waist down after a highway accident in Australia.
- A nurse in Cairo died of fright after opening a morgue in Egypt and discovering a "corpse" chanting prayers from the Quran.
- Southeast Asian currencies tumbled as the Philippine move to devalue its currency sparked worries that the crisis which engulfed the baht and the peso may widen to more of the region's currencies.
- Turmoil in the regional currency markets exacted its toll on the Singapore bourse, with the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index falling to its lowest level in two-and-a-half years.
- Era Realty Network, one of the largest estate agencies in the Housing Board resale market, is no longer on the board's Listed Housing Agents Scheme.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:
- Singapore Airlines will look into making its shares more affordable by splitting them into smaller units of less than $1 par value.
- There was little change in the situation faced by regional stock markets, with investors here shrugging off Friday's budget and sending the market to a new 30-month low.
- Only four of 24 brands managed to chalk up growth in the competitive car market in the first six months of this year.
- Rooms at gambling hot spot Genting Highlands are going for a rock bottom $1 a night to Singaporeans in a special offer.
- Keppel Corp shares fell after it announced plans to raise S$504.53 million in a redeemable convertible cumulative preference share issue.
- Malaysia's national oil firm Petroliam National Bhd announced a 44.7 percent year-on-year rise in group pre-tax profits to M$12.39 billion for the year to March.

- Construction and property firm Koh Brothers Group has consolidated the assets of its three main Singapore companies into its soon-to-be-listed building materials and equipment arm, G&W Group Holdings.
- OUB has scored a first for a Singapore bank by taking a lead manager role for the privatisation of Melbourne Airport.
- Jardine International Motor Holdings Ltd said there has been no specific event to warrant Friday's sharp fall in its stock.
-- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
